notes_for_editor: Early history rests on Free Press transcriptions at Gabriola Museum plus LighthouseFriends (which draws on Graham's Keepers of the Light, not read directly). Lens and fog-signal dates (1891, 1894, 1905, 1915, 1921) are LighthouseFriends only. The 1902 Marine report rescue row (scan p.321) was matched by position: its date column reads July 10, 1901 versus LighthouseFriends July 1902. Keepers after 1985 (Douglas, Beukens, Borgens, Quiring, Murrell, Matko) omitted from the roster as possibly living. Marine reports mention 'Entrance Island' for Quatsino Sound too (1907, 1910, 1916, 1923-24 fog alarm); not used. Clark's tenure end (1911 vs 1913) and Pilcher/Milne years conflict between sources. Record height 14.4 m vs 12.8 m (statement) vs 14 m (LF). Tyee says fully automated since late 90s, but CCG says staffed. Fact-check 2026-10-27: rescue row (scan p.321, printed p.144) confirmed from page image: M. G. Clark and John Roberts, July 10, 1901, binocular glass each.
